A patch to v0.3.0. A user is switched off and on again from the user drawer
and in bulk from the list, and a panel installed without a domain adds nodes
again. 8 commits since v0.3.0.

## Fixed

- **A user is switched off and back on from the user drawer** (A-294), a
  regression of v0.3.0: the switch was lost when the drawer was rebuilt.
  An expired or spent user stays so until it is extended or reset, and the
  drawer says so. Ticked rows of the user list are switched off or on in bulk,
  after a confirmation that names the count; the result is read from the
  server's report, and the audit log names each bulk row's target.
- **A panel installed without a domain adds nodes** (A-295). The payload a
  node is installed from is built by one function for both ways it leaves the
  panel, the node create window and the bootstrap token, and now always
  carries the panel's fingerprint and the heartbeat credentials, so the agent
  starts. A panel without https prints the `--payload-file` command instead of
  a bootstrap token the installer refuses, and its node window leads with the
  payload: download it, copy it to `/root/iceslab-node.payload`, run the
  command. The payload is handed out once, when the node is created. The node
  windows say that the panel issues the node's certificate and key and the
  token only fetches them, with no copy kept.

## Upgrading

The agent and the database are unchanged since v0.3.0: deploy the panel as
usual; there is no migration, and nodes that run need nothing for this
release.

A node added on v0.3.0 from the payload of its create window (downloaded or
pasted, installed with `--payload-file`) never started: that payload lacked
the panel's fingerprint. Nodes installed with a bootstrap token are not
affected. After the update:

- on a panel with https, re-issue the node's install token on its page and
  run the printed command on the VPS, adding `--reset` (or answering yes when
  the installer asks to wipe the previous install);
- on a panel without https, delete the node and create it again: the panel
  hands a payload out only when a node is created and keeps no node key.
  Download the new payload, copy it to the VPS and run the printed command
  with `--reset`.

## Known limitations

- A node installed on the same server as the panel shows as unreachable: the node's firewall lets the agent port in only from the panel's public address, and on one host the panel connects from its Docker network. Allow that network on the node, for example `ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port <agent port> proto tcp`. 172.16.0.0/12 covers Docker's default networks; the panel's own one is printed on the panel by
  `docker network inspect -f '{{range .IPAM.Config}}{{.Subnet}}{{end}}' $(docker inspect -f '{{range $n, $_ := .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{$n}}{{end}}' iceslab-prod-backend)`.
- With an entry pool size set, a user is given that many nodes of each profile, not of each country, so a profile served from several countries can hand a user nodes in one country only. Use one profile per country, or a pool size that covers every node of the profile.
- If the panel's database refuses a write during a traffic poll, the traffic that poll read from cores that reset their counters on each read (Hysteria and others) is not counted. This happens only on database errors and undercounts, never overcounts.
- REALITY on port 443 can connect worse than a non-standard port on some mobile networks in Russia; the defaults are unchanged in v0.3.1. If clients on mobile data fail on a REALITY host at 443, give that profile a second host on another port.
- The agent does not update itself: after a panel deploy, rebuild it on each
  node over SSH.
